title: Munna Point

bikeon.heading: Munna Point
paras: Munna Point, where the river bends at the end of Gympie Terrace, was noted by an early settler as a camping and fishing place and a corroboree ground for Aboriginal people. In 1871 it fell inside a reserve for Aboriginal mission purposes, which was cancelled in 1878; in the early 1900s most Kabi Kabi people were forcibly moved inland to Barambah, now Cherbourg. A public purposes reserve followed in 1884, and holiday camping began around 1929, when the new bridges brought cars. In 1956 part of the reserve was set aside for caravans and camping. When camping ended at Noosa Woods in 1990, Munna Point became the last camping ground on the estuary. In 2009 the park was entered on the Queensland Heritage Register as a good example of the waterside camping reserves that shaped holidays on this coast.

bikeon.text: Munna Point was recorded by early settlers as an Aboriginal camping, fishing and corroboree place. Just a little further along the point is the riverside caravan park. Holidaymakers have pitched tents there since about 1929, when the new bridges first brought cars to Noosa. Since camping ended at Noosa Woods in 1990, it has been the last camping ground on the river, and it is now on the Queensland Heritage Register.

story: Munna Point, where the river bends at the end of Gympie Terrace, was noted by an early settler as a camping and fishing place, and a corroboree ground for Aboriginal people.
In 1871 it fell inside a reserve for an Aboriginal mission, which was cancelled in 1878. In the early 1900s most Kabi Kabi people were forcibly moved inland to Barambah, now called Cherbourg.

Just a little further along the point is the caravan park. Holiday camping began there around 1929, when the new bridges brought cars, and part of the reserve was set aside for caravans in 1956. When camping ended at Noosa Woods in 1990, Munna Point became the last camping ground on the estuary.
In 2009 the park joined the Queensland Heritage Register, as a fine example of the waterside camping reserves that shaped holidays on this coast.
